page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-1xCPU-8GB is a virtual server based on the KVM hypervisor, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features a single shared vCPU derived from an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz, with one physical core and one thread. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, translating to an 8.0 GB per core allocation. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates that this server is positioned at the lower end of the performance spectrum. The single shared vCPU results in poor CPU performance, with a stress-ng score of 742.09 and a PassMark CPU score of 2006.22, both falling in the bottom 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 16.01 GB/sec and write speeds at 13.83 GB/sec. However, the system achieves average performance in single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression at 24.25 GB/sec and a Geekbench single-core score of 1247.0.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, making it a budget-friendly option for memory-intensive but compute-light workloads. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which limits multi-threaded performance and database operations, as evidenced by a poor PassMark database score of 653.28 and a low Redis SET throughput of 1.33 million operations per second. This configuration is best suited for lightweight background services, basic web serving, single-threaded utility scripts, or development environments that require a larger memory footprint without demanding sustained CPU performance.
